column1: # How scripts/qa-changed.bash (src-go/qa/changed) routes a changed file to checks: the
# classification as data. Loaded strictly; a short row, an unknown phase, check, predicate or
# flag is exit 2 naming the line. The directory trees a rule honours are scripts/qa-trees.tsv.
# phase <TAB> match <TAB> checks <TAB> flags          (columns are tab-separated)
# phase
#   also    every matching row applies, in order, and none stops the others
#   first   the first matching row classifies the file and ends the search
#   post    after every file is classified, when any file matched the kind: any:@sh, any:@py
#   perfile-gate  not a rule: the qa-*.bash gates that scripts/qa-gates.tsv lists which are NOT suites
#                 (run per file above, run whole as a gate, or inspecting the host)
# match
#   comma-separated globs with bash `case` semantics: a star matches any run of characters
#   including a slash, so *.bash matches at any depth. Or a predicate: @py (.py or a Python
#   shebang), @pytemplate (a .j2 with a Python shebang), @sh (.sh/.bash or a shell shebang),
#   @listed:<file> (a path that begins a line of that file; the file is read relative to the scripts directory).
# checks
#   comma-separated check ids, - for none, or @yaml (a first row only): the playbook / task /
#   vars logic, which computes the playbook set and so stays code. unit-tests on a Python file
#   adds the mirrored unit test module, not the file.
# flags
#   - for none, or comma-separated:
#     covered       a file the row handles counts as covered
#     closure       the file joins the src-go list whose Go build closure picks suites
#     tree:shell|python   skip (a first row reports "skipped") a file in that excluded tree
#     rel:<dir>     the tool is given the path with this prefix stripped
# Order is the contract. The src-go row precedes the YAML row so src-go/.golangci.yml runs the
# go check (go-qa run --changed); a Python script with a shell word in its shebang is Python because @py precedes @sh.
# The Go tests execute these files as parity references, so a change to one must run the Go gate.

# floor of src-go/go.mod; it runs whole when either, its wrapper, its Go package or command, or the

# support file (the YAML logic in classify.go), and when anything it reads changes: the gate table
# and the trees table (the inventory check and the scan), the shared discovery and gate loader, the
# Go module's own dependencies, its wrapper, its Go package or command, or the wrapper library.
also

# its rule, fixtures, script, Go package, command, the shared
# discovery or the trees table change; the .semgrep files are its own data and count as covered.

# The plan-script-logging gate judges the shell scripts and the logs/ directories of the active
# plans, and runs whole when one changes or is deleted, or its own script, Go package, command or
# the shared discovery (whose shell-shebang predicate it uses) change. It reads no fixture: its
# controls are Go tests, which the go check runs for a src-go change. The glob is deliberately wider
# than the gate (the matcher's * crosses /): a shell file under Completed/ or the plan tooling runs
# it too, though it reads neither. The walk is cheap, so the over-match is pinned, not narrowed.
